name: IAM AI

card.question: Can we trust who signed in?
card.title: IAM AI: continuous trust for every sign-in
card.description: Scoring every Microsoft Entra ID sign-in for risk, with rules that decide, models that advise, one policy that has the final say, and an explanation for every block. What I designed, what I got wrong, and what checking it found. Start with Part 1.

excerpts.1: A sign-in is checked once. Trust should be checked every time something changes. What IAM AI does, the four rules it is built on, and how 8,300 lines with no tests became something I could check.
excerpts.2: Eleven rules, three anomaly models and one hard floor. Why the model can never block on its own, and the inverted sign that quietly turned 45% of every score upside down.
excerpts.3: The scorer produces a number. A policy decides what happens. Why OPA has the final say, what happens when OPA is down, and why the language model only ever explains.
excerpts.4: The Docker images built, the type checker was clean and CI was green. Nobody had ever started the whole system. What running it found, and the design rules I took from it.
excerpts.5: Who owns this sign-in, this baseline, this verdict? Adding tenants to a system built without them, the leak that survived the fix, what is still open, and where Agent Sentinel joins in.
